title: $2 million secured for farmworker & senior housing in Half Moon Bay
location_name: Senior & Farmworker Housing project
summary: Senator Becker secured $2 million in the state budget to help build affordable housing for Half Moon Bay's farmworker and senior residents. The funds support the Senior and Farmworker Housing project at 555 Kelly Avenue.

title: $4.45 million secured to convert a parking lot into a downtown park
location_name: New downtown public park (former parking lot)
summary: Becker secured $4.45 million in the state budget to help turn a downtown parking lot into a new public park next to the Redwood City Public Library. He presented the funding to city officials in November 2022.

title: $2 million secured to replace the Newell Road Bridge
location_name: Newell Road Bridge (over San Francisquito Creek)
summary: Becker secured $2 million in the state budget to help replace the Newell Road Bridge, an aging span classified as functionally obsolete that links Palo Alto and East Palo Alto over San Francisquito Creek.

title: $2 million secured for a permanent Black History Museum
location_name: Domini Hoskins Black History Museum
summary: Becker negotiated $2 million in state funds to help the Domini Hoskins Black History Museum move from a pop-up to a permanent home. He presented the funding to the museum's leaders in Redwood City in February 2024.

title: $1.5 million secured for a Mountain View social-services agency
location_name: Community Services Agency (CSA) of Mountain View
summary: Becker secured $1.5 million in state funds for the Community Services Agency of Mountain View, Los Altos and Los Altos Hills, which provides social services to local families. He presented the check at the agency's Mountain View headquarters.

title: $4.5 million secured for home electrification in Menlo Park
location_name: City of Menlo Park electrification program
summary: Becker secured $4.5 million in the state budget to help Menlo Park electrify homes and municipal buildings — replacing gas appliances with electric ones — starting in the Belle Haven neighborhood. He presented the funds to the City Council in November 2022.

title: $1 million secured for entrepreneurship and job training in South San Francisco
location_name: City of South San Francisco
summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2022 state budget for South San Francisco to fund programs across North San Mateo County that support entrepreneurship, help small businesses, and provide job training for unemployed and underemployed residents.

title: $500,000 secured for a construction-trades apprenticeship program in San Mateo County
location_name: San Mateo County Union Community Alliance
summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2022 state budget for the San Mateo County Union Community Alliance's 20-week Trades Introduction Program, which helps women, people of color, and other underrepresented residents enter green construction trades, with support such as transportation and childcare.

title: $5 million secured for JobTrain's Center for Economic Mobility in East Palo Alto
location_name: JobTrain Center for Economic Mobility
summary: Becker secured $5 million in the 2021 state budget to help build JobTrain's new Center for Economic Mobility in East Palo Alto, a facility for job training, workforce services, and youth and early-childhood programs. The state funds were matched by a grant from the Emerson Collective.

title: $500,000 secured to repair the Pacifica Pier
location_name: Pacifica Municipal Pier
summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2021 state budget to repair the Pacifica Pier, fixing damaged railings and deterioration so the popular fishing and recreation pier could stay open to the public.

title: $1 million secured for senior affordable housing in North Fair Oaks
location_name: Alta Housing North Fair Oaks Senior Housing Project
summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for pre-development costs of Alta Housing's North Fair Oaks senior affordable housing project, to be built on land the nonprofit already owns in the North Fair Oaks area near Redwood City.

title: $300,000 secured for park and community projects in Millbrae
location_name: Bayside Manor and Marina Vista Park
summary: Becker secured $300,000 in the 2023 state budget for the City of Millbrae to support its Bayside Manor and Marina Vista Park projects, working alongside Assemblymember Diane Papan.

title: $300,000 secured for a youth anti-antisemitism fellowship in Palo Alto
location_name: Oshman Family Jewish Community Center
summary: Becker secured $300,000 in the 2023 state budget for the Oshman Family Jewish Community Center in Palo Alto to run its PREP Fellowship, a pilot program preparing teens to counter antisemitism before they head to college.

title: $200,000 secured for a Redwood City youth-opportunity program
location_name: Redwood City Together (PACE program)
summary: Becker secured $200,000 in the 2023 state budget for Redwood City Together's PACE program, which provides mentoring, activities, and support to local 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or work.

title: $1 million secured to fix flood protection for Redwood City mobile home parks
location_name: Redwood City mobile home park flood protection (with OneShoreline)
summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for Redwood City and the county's OneShoreline agency to repair and reinforce flood protections for mobile home parks that had flooded repeatedly because of undersized, failing pumps.

title: $1 million secured for water recycling in Burlingame
location_name: City of Burlingame wastewater reclamation project
summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for the City of Burlingame to reclaim wastewater and cut demand for drinking water, helping the city prepare for future droughts.

title: $200,000 secured for solar streetlights and greener infrastructure in Los Altos
location_name: City of Los Altos / GreenTown Los Altos
summary: Becker secured $200,000 in the 2023 state budget for the City of Los Altos, with GreenTown Los Altos, to move toward greener infrastructure and convert streetlights — one of the city's biggest energy users — to solar.

title: State funding restored for the Burlingame Broadway rail crossing
location_name: Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project
summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after it was cut, keeping funding on track for priority Peninsula grade-separation projects — including Burlingame's Broadway crossing, long ranked among California's most dangerous.

title: State funding restored for the Mountain View Caltrain crossing
location_name: Mountain View Caltrain Grade Separation Project
summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after a proposed cut, keeping priority Peninsula grade-separation projects — including Mountain View's Caltrain crossing — eligible to move toward construction and draw federal matching funds.

title: State funding restored for Palo Alto's rail grade separation
location_name: Connecting Palo Alto Rail Grade Separation Project
summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after a proposed cut, keeping the Connecting Palo Alto grade-separation project eligible for state funding and federal matching dollars.

title: $2 million helped complete East Palo Alto's first regulation football field
location_name: East Palo Alto regulation football field
summary: As Bay Area Caucus chair, Becker helped secure the final $2 million needed to complete East Palo Alto's first regulation-size football field, a roughly $4 million community project that broke ground in September 2025.

title: Free tuition at San Mateo County's community colleges (Cañada, CSM, Skyline)
location_name: San Mateo County Community College District
summary: Becker authored SB 893 (2022), a state law letting the San Mateo County Community College District use local funds to eliminate tuition at Cañada College, College of San Mateo, and Skyline College. His follow-up SB 968, signed in 2026, made the free-college program permanent.

title: Helped double state funding for Bay Area shoreline flood protection ($102 million)
location_name: Bay Area coastal & shoreline resilience
summary: As Bay Area Caucus chair, Becker helped secure a doubling of state funding — to $102 million — for coastal and bay shoreline flood-protection projects across the Bay Area in the 2025 budget, in a county considered California's most vulnerable to shoreline flooding.

title: $500,000 secured toward the 90-mile Ohlone-Portolá Heritage Trail
location_name: Ohlone-Portolá Heritage Trail (San Mateo County)
summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2023 state budget toward creating the roughly 90-mile Ohlone-Portolá Heritage Trail, which would trace a historic route across San Mateo County. Because it spans the whole county, it's listed here rather than as a single map pin.

title: 200 laptops distributed to East Palo Alto students to close the digital divide
location_name: East Palo Alto laptop distribution (with AT&T, StreetCode Academy, Human-I-T)
summary: In 2025, Senator Becker worked with AT&T, StreetCode Academy, and Human-I-T to distribute 200 laptops to East Palo Alto students and families. The aim was to help close the digital divide, so students without a computer at home aren't left behind on schoolwork or job applications.

title: Celebrated 10 years of the Genentech–South San Francisco schools STEM partnership
location_name: Genentech (Futurelab / SSFUSD partnership)
summary: Senator Becker joined educators, community leaders, and Genentech employees in South San Francisco to celebrate the 10th anniversary of Futurelab. The program is a long-running partnership between Genentech and the South San Francisco Unified School District that gives local students hands-on STEM education.
